title: A Brave Pawn Runs: Spend the Tempo on Promotion
summary: Push the remote passer before the bishop can attack it; compare the source’s separate pawn-mate finish.

nodes.question: The queen and rook have disappeared. Which pawn matters now?
nodes.explanation: White has Kc8, b5 and h6 versus Kb6, Bd5 and d7. The bishop cannot control the dark promotion square h8, but can still attack h7 if White wastes a move.

nodes.question: In a different source branch, how can a pawn mate a king with a queen?
nodes.explanation: Begin separately after ...Bxa6 at 109 seconds. White has Kc7, b5 and h6 versus Ka7, Qa8, Ba6 and d7. The black queen and bishop occupy the king’s own flight squares.

branches.title: Source ending: advance the remote passer
commentary: Begin after ...Kb6 at 79 seconds in the complete six-piece ending. The earlier nine-piece sacrifice sequence is outside this exact verification.
h7 spends the move on the passer and keeps a forced White win. The bishop on d5 cannot attack h8, and the king is too far away to stop promotion immediately.
Kb5 is the source’s illustrated king move. It leaves the b-pawn in place and does not catch the h-pawn.
h8=Q promotes. White has a checked winning queen ending against bishop and pawn, with b5 still present. Further conversion is left to practice; this is not immediate mate.
branches.explanation: h8=Q promotes. White has a checked winning queen ending against bishop and pawn, with b5 still present. Further conversion is left to practice; this is not immediate mate.

branches.title: Independent defense: bring the bishop toward the passer
commentary: An independently selected representative bishop reply tests whether the bishop can stop the advanced h-pawn.
h7 acts before Black can establish a useful attack on h7.
Be6 approaches the pawn along a light-square diagonal, but h8 is a dark square and is not controlled by this bishop. This defense still loses with best play.
h8=Q promotes safely and retains the exact White win. The bishop’s square color matters here because White has already secured the pawn’s final advance.

branches.title: Independent error: collect d7 first
commentary: An independently selected comparison tests a tempting capture before advancing h6.
Kxd7 removes a black pawn but gives up the forced win. White has allowed time for the bishop to attack the h-pawn’s next square.
Be4 controls h7 along e4-f5-g6-h7 and holds a draw with best play. A wrong-color bishop for h8 can still stop a pawn before it reaches promotion.
h7 now steps onto the bishop’s diagonal. This selected continuation remains drawn; White no longer has the immediate winning race.
Bxh7 removes the h-pawn. The exact bishop-versus-b-pawn ending is drawn. The important error was spending the first tempo on Kxd7, not merely the final pawn capture.

branches.title: Separate source branch: a pawn closes the cage
commentary: Begin separately after ...Bxa6 at 109 seconds, a complete seven-piece diagram. This is not a continuation of the six-piece queen-sacrifice branch shown by the other lines.

b6# checks Ka7. Kc7 controls b6, b7 and b8; Black’s own Ba6 and Qa8 occupy a6 and a8. Neither piece can capture the pawn on b6 or interpose against its adjacent check. Black has no escape and is checkmated.

exercises.prompt: Why must White push h7 before capturing d7?
exercises.answer: Taking d7 gives Black ...Be4, which controls h7 before the pawn can advance safely. Immediate h7 wins the race because the bishop cannot control h8.

exercises.prompt: How can a queen fail to prevent a pawn mate?
exercises.answer: The queen on a8 occupies a king flight square and cannot capture b6. White’s king protects the checking pawn and covers the b-file escapes; Black’s own bishop blocks a6.

The larger original promotion/rook-sacrifice setup is source context outside exact verification. The bishop-defense and wasted-capture comparisons are independently selected; the two source branches are not joined into an invented legal sequence.
